The undocumented 'icebp' instruction (aka 'int1') works pretty much like
'int3' in the absense of in-circuit probing equipment (except
obviously
column2: that it raises #DB instead of raising #BP)

column1: some validation test-suites as such.
But Andy Lutomirski noticed that his test suite acted differently in kvm
than on bare hardware.
The reason is that kvm used an inexact test for the icebp instruction:
it just assumed that an all-zero VM exit qualification value meant that
the VM exit was due to icebp.
That is not unlike the guess that do_debug() does for the actual
exception handling case
rule.  do_debug() does it because it wants to ascribe _some_ reasons to
the #DB that happened
column2: and an empty %dr6 value means that 'icebp' is the

column1: most likely casue and we have no better information.
But kvm can just do it right
actually sees the real reason for the #DB in the VM-exit interruption
information field.
So instead of relying on an inexact heuristic
exit information that says ""it was 'icebp'"".
Right now the 'icebp' instruction isn't technically documented by Intel
but that will hopefully change.  The special ""privileged software
exception"" information _is_ actually mentioned in the Intel SDM
though the cause of it isn't enumerated.
